land.text: Tumapel (present-day Malang), where Ken Arok 'rose from being a servant of Tunggul Ametung, a regional ruler in Tumapel'; Kediri itself became a fief

predecessors.note: Tumapel was a district of the Kediri kingdom; Kediri's whole realm passed under Singhasari in 1222 (vassal relation in the ledger).

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps the Singhasari row to 1293; the Singhasari page's infobox puts the Jayakatwang rebellion in 1292.

land.text: Raden Vijaya 'ascended the throne as Kertajasa Jayawardhana, the first king of the great Majapahit Empire, on 12 November 1293'

successors.note: Majapahit follows Kediri's brief restoration, not Singhasari directly.

capitals.name: Tumapel / Kutaraja Singhasari (Malang)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Tumapel, later called Kutaraja Singhasari (modern outskirt Malang)'. The page dates the renaming nowhere.

rulers.name: Ken Arok (Rajasa)
rulers.note: Infobox dates; the Ken Arok page agrees (reign 1222-1227, died 1227).

rulers.name: Visnuvardhana
rulers.note: The page's body text gives 'Vishnuvardhana-Narasimhamurti 1248-1268', which conflicts with the infobox dates for Tohjaya and Visnuvardhana.

rulers.name: Kertanagara
rulers.note: 'reigning from 1268 to 1292' (Kertanagara page); killed in May or June 1292.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1227 shape held back to the founding: Ken Arok's Tumapel (Singasari, 'about 50 kilometres east of Kediri') with Kediri as a fief ('Kediri became a fief under the kingdom of Singasari')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts Singhasari in 1227 (Ken Arok's death) and keeps the 73,225 km2 Kediri shape under Kediri until 1226; the page founds Singhasari in 1222. The pages give no extent for 1222-1226; the 1227 shape (identical to Kediri's 1139 shape) is the best outline and is read as Tumapel plus the Kediri fief. No area on the page.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, but its Kediri part is a fief, drawn as vassal land of Singhasari from 1222 to 1292 (ledger vassal events), not as direct territory: 'Kediri became a fief under the kingdom of Singasari'

keyframe_review.note: Status only: 73,225 km2, the Kediri shape of 1139-1226 carried on (286 cells, identical). Which part was ruled directly from Tumapel and which part stayed under a Kediri line is not on the pages; the page gives no infobox area to compare.

correction.text: the 1285 shape with Bali added as vassal land: 'In 1284, he subjected nearby Bali to vassalage', and ending in 1292, not 1293, when Kertanagara was killed

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1285 growth (73,225 to 78,238 km2) is 17 grid cells covering the island of Madura (112.7 to 114.0 E, around Sumenep in the east), not Bali: Bali's 24 cells lie in no Singhasari shape. The pages give Bali (1284, vassalage) and, undated, Madura ('Other areas in Madura Island and Borneo also offered their submission'; Arya Viraraja, regent of Sumenep), so Madura is kept and Bali added. No infobox area to compare; the shape runs to 1293, a year after the state's end.

region.text: Tumapel / Singasari, now in Malang municipality

ledger.note: 1222: Ken Arok defeats Kertajaya of Kediri at Ganter and founds Singhasari at Tumapel. 'In 1222, at the battle of Ganter, he defeated King Kertajaya of Kediri and founded the new kingdom of Singasari.' 'His new kingdom was centered in Singasari (now in Malang municipality), about 50 kilometres east of Kediri.' The Singhasari page's infobox: 'Battle of Genter: 1222'. Cliopatria starts the polity in 1227.

region.text: the Kediri kingdom: 'Kediri became a fief under the kingdom of Singasari'

ledger.note: 1222: Kediri becomes Singhasari's fief. 'Kediri became a fief under the kingdom of Singasari.' The page does not say whether Kertajaya's line kept a local throne; Cliopatria draws the same land as Singhasari's own from 1227.

region.text: Bali: 'In 1284, he subjected nearby Bali to vassalage'

ledger.note: 1284: Kertanegara subjects Bali. 'In 1284, he subjected nearby Bali to vassalage.' The Singhasari page: 'In the year 1284, King Kertanegara led a hostile Pabali expedition to Bali.' The Bali Kingdom page: 'This expedition seems to have integrated Bali into Singhasari's realm' (vassal or part of the realm; the Bali dossier records a loss). No Cliopatria Singhasari shape contains Bali.

region.text: Madura, the 17 cells Cliopatria adds in 1285: 'Other areas in Madura Island and Borneo also offered their submission to Kertanagara'

ledger.note: c. 1285: Madura joins Singhasari (year is Cliopatria's; the page gives none). 'Other areas in Madura Island and Borneo also offered their submission to Kertanagara.' The Singhasari page names Arya Viraraja as 'a regent from Sumenep on the island of Madura'. No state is named on Madura.

region.text: 'The Melayu Kingdom in eastern Sumatra came under control' (the page names no province; Jambi is the Melayu heartland)

ledger.note: c. 1290: the Pamalayu expedition brings Melayu under Singhasari. 'Around 1290, he launched the Pamalayu expedition to Sumatra'; 'The Melayu Kingdom in eastern Sumatra came under control'. The Singhasari page dates the launch to 1275 ('In the year 1275, King Kertanegara... launched a naval campaign toward the weak remains of the Srivijaya', led by Admiral Mahesa Anabrang); the page does not say when Melayu submitted. The region is the Melayu heartland read as Jambi.

region.text: the realm of Singhasari at its fall, taken by Jayakatwang of Kediri; Cliopatria's 1293 shape (Java with Madura, without Bali)

ledger.note: 1292: Jayakatwang of Kediri overthrows Singhasari. Infobox 'Jayakatwang rebellion: 1292'; 'The Kediri (Gelang-gelang) army attacked Singhasari simultaneously from both north and south'; 'Jayakatwang usurped and killed Kertanagara during the Tantra sacred ceremony.' The Kertanagara page dates the killing to 'May or June 1292'.

region.text: the Kediri kingdom: 'Kediri became a fief under the kingdom of Singasari'

ledger.note: 1292: the fief of Kediri ends when its ruler Jayakatwang rebels and kills Kertanagara (infobox 'Jayakatwang rebellion: 1292'); the Kediri Kingdom article, cited in the kediri-kingdom dossier, has 'In 1292, Jayakatwang rebelled against Singhasari'.

region.text: Bali, independent again after Singhasari's fall

ledger.note: 1292: Bali is free again. 'After Singhasari fell in 1292, once again Balinese rulers enjoyed their independence from Java.'

region.text: 'The Melayu Kingdom in eastern Sumatra came under control' (the page names no province; Jambi is the Melayu heartland)

ledger.note: 1292: Singhasari's overlordship of Melayu ends with the kingdom. The pages are silent on what happened to Melayu or the expedition; the year is the state's end year.

region.text: the realm of Singhasari at its fall, taken by Jayakatwang of Kediri; Cliopatria's 1293 shape (Java with Madura, without Bali)

ledger.note: 1292: Kertanagara dies and Singhasari ends. 'Kertanagara was killed along with many courtiers in his palace in Singhasari in May or June 1292.' The Singhasari page: Raden Vijaya forced the Mongols out on 31 May 1293 and 'ascended the throne as Kertajasa Jayawardhana, the first king of the great Majapahit Empire, on 12 November 1293'; Cliopatria keeps the row to 1293.

wars.name: Battle of Ganter

zones.text: the Kediri kingdom: 'Kediri became a fief under the kingdom of Singasari'

wars.outcome: Ken Arok of Tumapel defeats Kertajaya and founds Singhasari; Kediri becomes a fief.
wars.note: 'In 1222, at the battle of Ganter, he defeated King Kertajaya of Kediri and founded the new kingdom of Singasari.'

wars.name: Pamalayu expedition

zones.text: 'The Melayu Kingdom in eastern Sumatra came under control' (the page names no province; Jambi is the Melayu heartland)

wars.outcome: A Javanese naval expedition to Sumatra under Admiral Mahesa Anabrang; Melayu came under Singhasari control, the 'weak remains of the Srivijaya' being the target.
wars.note: Dates conflict: the Singhasari page has 'In the year 1275', the Kertanagara page 'Around 1290'. The span runs from the earlier launch to the kingdom's fall; the Srivijaya dossier (se-02-a) puts a Singhasari occupation of Palembang in 1288-1293.

wars.name: Bali expedition of 1284
wars.outcome: Bali subjected to vassalage (Kertanagara page) or integrated into the realm (Bali Kingdom page); independent again in 1292.
wars.note: Singhasari page: 'In the year 1284, King Kertanegara led a hostile Pabali expedition to Bali.'

wars.name: Mongol demand for tribute
wars.outcome: Kertanagara refused tribute in 1289 and disfigured the Mongol envoy; the Mongol fleet reached Tuban in early 1293, after his death, and was used and then expelled by Raden Vijaya.
wars.note: 'in 1289, the last envoy was sent to demand the same, and King Kertanegara refused to pay tribute'; the envoy is named Meng Ki on the page. No border moved.

wars.name: Jayakatwang's revolt

zones.text: the realm of Singhasari at its fall, taken by Jayakatwang of Kediri; Cliopatria's 1293 shape (Java with Madura, without Bali)

wars.outcome: Jayakatwang kills Kertanagara and holds the realm for about a year as restored Kediri; Singhasari ends.
wars.note: 'The Kediri (Gelang-gelang) army attacked Singhasari simultaneously from both north and south.'

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary; the extent beyond Tumapel is Cliopatria's. Bali and the Melayu vassalage rest on expedition accounts, not frontiers.

sources.title: Singhasari
sources.note: Identity, capital, rulers, Pamalayu 1275, Bali 1284, Mongol demand 1289, Jayakatwang 1292, Majapahit 1293. No area in the infobox.

sources.title: Kertanagara
sources.note: Reign, Bali 1284, Melayu c. 1290, Madura and Borneo submissions, death in May or June 1292.

sources.title: Ken Arok
sources.note: Ganter 1222, the fief of Kediri, the centre at Singasari.

sources.title: Bali Kingdom
sources.note: Bali under Singhasari in 1284 and independent after 1292; Airlangga's brothers on the Balinese throne.

notes: Page budget 1-2 pages, four used: the Singhasari page leaves the founding (1222) and the Bali tie to pages that were open for the Kediri dossier. Cliopatria rows: Singhasari 1227-1293 should be 1222-1292; its first shape is Kediri's 1139 shape carried on unchanged, and its 1285 growth is Madura, not Bali. Disagreements: Pamalayu 1275 (Singhasari page) versus around 1290 (Kertanagara page); reigns of Tohjaya and Visnuvardhana (infobox 1248-1250 and 1250-1268, body text 1248-1268); Ken Arok's dates; the Bali dossier (se-02-a) records a 1284 loss to Singhasari where this one records vassalage, and the Srivijaya dossier records an occupation of Palembang from 1288. Not settled: which of the old Kediri land was directly ruled; undated submissions of Borneo (Balakana/Bakulapura), the Maluku (Gurun) and the Sunda Kingdom ('possibly also gained control over the Sunda Kingdom'), and Pahang and the alliance with Champa, none given a year or a place on the pages; the pages say Madura's regent was Arya Viraraja of Sumenep without a date. States needing dossiers: melayu-kingdom (Melayu/Dharmasraya, Jambi). No new gazetteer names needed.
